They watched in amazement as she put one foot down, then the other… and slowly took a step! Soon, she was walking, and then running, as if nothing ever happened! Leibel quickly took out his phone to video the special moment.

Since they still had time before seeing the doctor, they took Sheina to the children’s play area. She played and jumped and ran like normal.

When it was their turn, the doctor was amazed. “Is this the same girl you brought in before?” he asked. “Well, you can go home now. The test results seem fine. I’ll give you medicine just in case.”

On their way home, their phone rang. It was the sofer. “I just finished checking the mezuzos,” he said. “They were all good— except for one. In that mezuzah, the letter “veis” in the word “ּובְלֶכְּתְָך” was too short, and the word looked like two separate words. I fixed it, and now it’s good as new.”

Leibel and Miri were speechless. “Wait,” they said, “what time did you fix it?”

The sofer thought for a moment. “I finished with that mezuzah about half an hour ago,” he said.

followed the hora’ah of checking their mezuzos, Sheina’s foot was healed in a miraculous way.

Sheina’s foot had completely healed from one moment to the next. What caused such a miraculous recovery?

My cousin Leibel and his wife, Miri, are shluchim in Ashkelon, Eretz Yisroel. One Shabbos morning, they awoke to the sound of a loud cry.

They rushed to her room and gasped. Sheina, who had already been walking for a few months, was struggling to simply stand up.

Each time, her little legs gave in and she fell to the floor. All she could do was crawl like a baby.

They rushed her to the hospital to make sure that she was okay. “Sheina isn’t in danger,” the doctor told them. “You can go back home and return after Shabbos for more tests.”

They walked back home, and Sheina spent the rest of Shabbos crawling around the house. Whenever she would try to stand, she just fell down. Everyone was very worried.

After Shabbos, Miri wrote a letter to the Rebbe and sent it to the Ohel, asking for a bracha that Sheina should get better.

She also took down all the mezuzos to be checked, because the Rebbe had told many people to do that when something was wrong.

When Leibel came back from Maariv, they dropped the mezuzos off at the sofer and took Sheina to the hospital. But there was a long line, and it was already late at night. Since the doctor had said that Sheina wasn’t in danger, they decided to go back home and try again in the morning.

The next day, they returned to the hospital. The doctor took some tests and told them to wait in the hallway for the results.

As they waited, Sheina looked up and said, “Abba, Ima, I can walk now! My feet only hurt a little bit!”
